profile.headline: Software Engineer Sr. II - Aero Software Engineer
profile.jobTitle: Software Engineer Sr. II - Aero Software Engineer
profile.summary:
Throughout my career, I have continually implemented various engineering, mathematical, managerial, business, and statistical principles to resolving complex problems by performing any necessary analyses, conducting ground or flight testing, and by leading the development of any necessary software programs in support of the warfighters’ strategic needs.  My experiences have allowed me to cross-train as an engineer/software developer/manager that has pioneered new predictive and cognitive capabilities in order to provide actionable results, insights, and recommendations.  

I have demonstrated leadership by implementing new engineering methodologies into the workflow by applying my knowledge in aerodynamics, acoustics, aero-acoustics, aero-heating, turbulent flows, maneuvering loads, and stress.  I have also led the efforts of others as a Senior Aerospace Engineer supporting weapons certifications/ flight clearances and as the Aeromechanical Design Chief for temporary test modifications (T-2 Mods). I have led multidisciplinary engineering (mechanical, electrical, aerospace, systems, computational) teams to accomplish strategic business, program, or scientific endeavors, and as a manager I also had the privilege of building and strengthening a team.

One of my notable technical achievements was an object-oriented generic loads software program, which fulfilled the one algorithm for all aircraft methodology for certifications and flight clearances.  In order to accomplish this task, I built a library of software objects driven by both engineering and mathematical definitions.  This strong foundation allowed me to define the data models and simulations necessary for an algorithm that solves for an infinite number of three-dimensional free-body diagrams.  This loads program coalesced software and engineering principles so that both disciplines are simultaneously optimized and expeditiously provide accurate answers.

positions.title: Software Engineer Sr. II - Aero Software Engineer
positions.description:
•Responsible for designing, developing, integrating and test of high fidelity, scalable, physics-based Aerodynamics Software models for Real-Time simulation training applications.
•Troubleshoot and fix existing software discrepancies in a variety of aerodynamic subsystems such as: engines, flight controls, control loading, motion, and aircraft systems.
•Provide aerodynamic software design, development and integration support on a variety of simulator programs for both helicopter and fixed wing platforms.
•Resolve pre-existing software discrepancies within the aero domain
•Support testing activity both in the lab and on the simulator to include flight test matching, qualification test guide (Client) analysis and certification testing.

positions.title: Senior Software Developer - Simulation Software Engineer
positions.description:
•Develop rapid prototype development simulations (RPDS) of on-board F-35 software, supporting environment, threats, in-flight phenomenon, and proposed capabilities for training and requirements refinement.
•Implemented numerical solution of a 3 DOF dynamic system for a smart munition through flight phases.
•Pioneered a statistical hit or miss model for a munition based on in-flight simulation parameters.
•Designed, coded, implemented new symbology state in OpenGL that represents new in-flight condition.

positions.title: Structures Engineer
positions.description:
•Provide direct fleet support of operational, maintenance-repair, and overhaul F-35 activities. Respond to Action Requests from services intended to solve F-35 sustainment issues. Review contractor provided sustainment solutions for continued airworthiness.  Performed statistical cross-correlation analysis to diagnose in-flight anomaly.
•Implemented an air data software program by deriving aerodynamic equations and developing user interface. Program allows easy visualization and generation of large data sets.

positions.title: Aeromechanical Design Chief
positions.description:
•Managed a team of 5 engineers and 3 technicians to design, analyze, and produce flightworthy modifications. Ensure technical accuracy of performed analysis by reviewing finite element analyses (FEA), and determine the applicability of inertial, aerodynamic, thermal, and dynamic loads. Review the design solutions proposed by team to ensure they are practical, flightworthy, ground tested, and can be manufactured in machine and sheet metal shops. Responsible for determining and providing any staffing, training, software, and hardware requirements.  Managed projects through complex multidisciplinary (mechanical, electrical, aerospace, systems, computational) requirements refinement process to ensure feasibility and airworthiness.
•Developed data and analytical models to meet business & engineering needs by developing software programs. This included the identification and integration of existing and new data needed to institutionalize data-driven analysis, and the application of tools and techniques to prepare and manipulate the data for analysis. In addition, developed software/architecture for managing the 896 Test Support Squadron projects (a database), and configuration control of aircraft equipment and corresponding mass properties.
•Coordinated with external organizations to implement the new DOD-wide airworthiness process.

positions.title: Senior Aerospace Engineer
positions.description:
•Lead aerodynamic, turbulent flow, acoustic, software development, and structural maneuver (static) loads subject matter expert. Founded the development and activation of in-house compatibility expertise to address weapon bay acoustics in Flight Clearances (FCs) and Certification Recommendations (CRs). Diagnosed aero-acoustic resonance issues on new configurations for the F-35 and B-1B. Pioneered all application tools and techniques to prepare and manipulate data for analysis, visualization, and reporting making in-house cavity flow acoustics engineering rationale possible for B-1B, F-35, and F-22. Communicated various complex quantitative analyses in a clear, precise, and actionable manner. Educated F-35 community (industry, government, and research lab) about existing resonant mechanisms responsible for tones in weapons bays, and creating flight test data based engineering models of tones. Constructed flight tests with intense loads and environmental conditions to demonstrate analyzed limits of aircraft-store combinations, and monitored instrumented loads aircraft when necessary to support FCs and CRs. Supported/defined technical efforts and methodologies necessary to safely certify (CRs and FCs) and test new aircraft-store combinations for F-22, F-35, A-10, F-15, F-16, F-117, B-1B, and QF-4 in the areas of maneuvering (static) loads, stress, thermal loads, and acoustics. Calculated aircraft state vectors and resulting inertial and aerodynamic loads for analysis to ensure loads are within previously cleared envelopes and/or stress index (S.I.) equation limits. Coordinated with weapon and aircraft manufacturers on analysis of airborne systems, and performed additional testing or analysis, when necessary, to the requested flight limits. 
•Lead engineer for a research and software development team of 3 engineers and 1 software developer. Developed, tested, and implemented ten state-of-the-art software tools in the Loads group toolbox (initially zero).

positions.title: Engineering Student Trainee (Co-op)
positions.description: •Three cooperative education tours at JSC in Operations, Engineering, and Safety, Reliability, and Quality Assurance (SR&QA). Worked at an arc-jet facility, which tested new materials for reentry into atmosphere. Managed two reentry test programs; ablative materials and X-38 heat shield. Simulated Orbiter ascent into low earth orbit given new wind velocities from weather balloon.
